contexts: case management files read by hand
reading: Enrolment is not random: the most complex frequent attenders are enrolled first, so a naive comparison makes the program look harmful (claim c2). Death and ICU admission are rare enough that a case-control design is efficient, provided controls are sampled from those still at risk (claim c5) and exposure is measured as enrolment before the index date (claim c3). Programme intensity differs between tertiary and community sites (claim c4), which matters as soon as more than one site is included.
